initiative: Los Angeles Guerilla Store
dates: Opening and closing dates not stated; article published 1 March 2008
what_happened: Temporary Comme des Garcons store at 125 West 4th Street, Suite 106, Los Angeles. The article describes the guerilla concept as a store that opens in a city for a set period and then closes for good. It was hard to find and sold exclusive CDG items, which the article does not list.
results_and_next_move: No results reported. Only US guerrilla store found with a dated page; no New York guerrilla store found. Source older than three years.

initiative: Seasonal one-day closure and reset of the West 22nd Street store
dates: Closed 5 August 2026 and reopened 6 August 2026 with Fall/Winter 2026 collections
what_happened: The Chelsea store at 520 West 22nd Street closed for a day and reopened with a refreshed interior, new displays, fixtures and the new season's merchandise. The page describes a gallery-like space in an art district. The page is partly behind a sign-up wall, so events or partners may exist that are not visible.
results_and_next_move: Cadence not confirmed for this store by the source. Inference: a 2019 Fzine piece on the Singapore store (https://www.fzine.com/fashion/comme-des-garcon-re-opens-its-doors-and-debuts-its-fw19-collection) describes occasional seasonal overhauls of CDG spaces, so a seasonal rhythm is plausible but unverified for New York.

initiative: Meg Webster sculpture installed in the West 22nd Street store
dates: On view in March 2026; opening and closing dates not stated
what_happened: Artist Meg Webster's 2017 salt sculpture Copper Containing Salt II was installed in the Chelsea store. The article notes Dia Chelsea sits directly across the street and that another Webster salt cylinder is at Dia Beacon. No opening event is described.
partners: Meg Webster (artist). Dia Art Foundation is named as a neighbour; its role in the installation is not stated.
results_and_next_move: No results reported. The article does not mention the perfume, which a separate source ties to Dia and Webster (see comme-des-garcons-05).

initiative: Parfums x Dia Art Foundation x Meg Webster fragrance
dates: Reported as available in March 2026; exact date not stated
what_happened: COMME des GARCONS Parfums released a 50 ml fragrance with the Dia Art Foundation and artist Meg Webster, in a tetrahedral box. It is sold at select stores and Dover Street Market locations in New York, Los Angeles, London, Paris and Tokyo. The same page reports Webster's sculpture on display at the West 22nd Street store.
physical_digital_bridge: Physical retail across five cities; online sale not mentioned
results_and_next_move: Price and sales not stated. Next move not found.

initiative: Kawakubo presentation at Independent art fair, Pier 36
what_happened: Rei Kawakubo showed more than twenty semi-unique body objects drawn from the past five years inside a rebar and coloured-plastic structure designed for the fair, running through its centre. HUBE reports each work in an edition of three or fewer with one version for sale, at prices reported between USD 9,000 and 30,000. Wallpaper (https://www.wallpaper.com/fashion-beauty/comme-des-garcons-independent-art-fair, 2026-05-16) describes 20 dresses selected by Kawakubo. RETAILBOSS calls it her first solo showing at a New York art fair and her first major New York presentation since the 2017 Met show.
objective: Not stated. Inference: reach art-world audiences and collectors.
partners: Independent art fair (founder Elizabeth Dee positioned it as a centrepiece)
physical_digital_bridge: Pieces sold on site; online link not mentioned
results_and_next_move: No sales volume or attendance reported. Next move not found.

initiative: Rei Kawakubo/Comme des Garcons: Art of the In-Between at the Met
dates: 4 May to 4 September 2017; Met Gala on 1 May 2017
what_happened: The Met Costume Institute showed about 140 examples of Kawakubo's womenswear from the early 1980s to her latest collection, in nine themes on in-betweenness. The Met calls it the first monographic show on a living designer since the 1983 Yves Saint Laurent exhibition. The page thanks Apple, Conde Nast, Farfetch, H&M, Maison Valentino and Warner Bros. for support.
partners: The Metropolitan Museum of Art Costume Institute (curator Andrew Bolton); sponsors listed above
results_and_next_move: Attendance not stated on the page. A 2026 source (RETAILBOSS) calls the Independent presentation her first major New York one since this show. Source older than three years.

initiative: CDG Pocket shop on Tenth Avenue
dates: Opened late August 2015 per Hypebeast (2015-08-31); duration not stated
what_happened: A new outpost at 112 Tenth Avenue in West Chelsea, about a six-minute walk from the original store. Time Out describes a no-frills grab-and-go space for cheaper accessories and fragrances, mostly Play items. Prices listed in 2015 included wallets at 210 dollars and the Play x Converse Chuck Taylor '70 at 125 dollars. Hypebeast calls it the first Pocket shop in the US (https://hypebeast.com/2015/8/comme-des-garcons-pocket-nyc).
audience: Not stated. Inference: shoppers seeking an accessible entry point.
results_and_next_move: Classification is a judgment call (store opening, not an event). Results not found. Inference: the 2021 Bloomingdale's Pocket shop (comme-des-garcons-09) suggests the format continued. Source older than three years.

initiative: CDG Pocket shop inside Bloomingdale's 59th Street
dates: Announced as open on 22 March 2021; duration not stated
what_happened: A 500 sq ft shop on the first floor of the Bloomingdale's flagship, using a black polka-dot curved plexiglass design by Kawakubo meant to feel like a convenience store. The article calls it the first US shop with this design. It stocks Pocket, Play, Play x Converse sneakers, wallets and fragrances including Rouge Parfum.
investment: Size 500 sq ft; capital not found
results_and_next_move: Results not found. Source older than three years.

initiative: Air Jordan 1 surprise drop at the New York flagship and DSM
dates: In-store release 2 August 2019; online preview about 7 August 2019
what_happened: The CDG x Air Jordan 1 went on sale in white and black at Dover Street Market New York and the CDG flagship at 345 dollars, without an official announcement. CDG press confirmed the details to Hypebeast. DSM later offered a limited online preview in sizes US 11 and 12, with a wider release expected in September.
physical_digital_bridge: In-store first, then limited online preview at DSM
results_and_next_move: Quantities and queues not reported. Wider release expected in September 2019 per the update; outcome not checked. Source older than three years.

initiative: PLAY Comme des Garcons x Converse Chuck Taylor
dates: First announced August 2009; repeated releases since
what_happened: Limited-edition Converse Chuck Taylor with the Play heart logo, high or low top, in black or white, at 90 euros. It went on sale in Japan first, then in CDG stores in New York, Paris, London, Hong Kong and Seoul and selected multi-brand retailers, from September 2009. Later pages show the line still sold in 2021 at Bloomingdale's (comme-des-garcons-09) and at DSM New York with its e-shop (https://newyork.doverstreetmarket.com/pages/play-cdg-x-converse-chuck-70, year not shown).
physical_digital_bridge: Stores first; later online via DSM e-shop and Converse.com per DSM New York
results_and_next_move: Longevity of more than 15 years is the visible result; no sales figures. Source older than three years.

initiative: CDG SHIRT x A$AP Nast capsule
dates: Launched 8 May 2025 at DSM New York; other DSM stores and online from 15 May 2025
what_happened: A 12-style capsule of T-shirts, cardigans and shirts with the musician's logo and graphics tied to his upcoming album. DSM says he is the first musician to customize existing CDG SHIRT styles. Dexter Navy shot the campaign, promoted through activations across DSM stores.
physical_digital_bridge: New York store first, then the DSMNY E-Shop and other DSM e-shops
results_and_next_move: Results not found. Source is DSM New York's own page.

initiative: CDG line launch with a dedicated worldwide online shop
dates: Stores from 27 October 2018; online shop from 1 November 2018
what_happened: The CDG line, with the CDG logo on apparel, accessories and footwear, launched in selected CDG and DSM stores including New York and Los Angeles, and through a dedicated online shop shipping worldwide. An update says it would not be at the Paris location, so retailer details are partly unclear.
objective: Not stated. Context: in 2015 Joffe said the main line was not sold online (https://anothermag.com/fashion-beauty/7806/adrian-joffe-on-social-media-and-e-commerce).
physical_digital_bridge: Dedicated CDG online shop launched alongside the store roll-out
results_and_next_move: Results not found. Inference: the accessible CDG line was the vehicle for the first brand-run online shop. Source older than three years.

initiative: Organic TikTok backlash against the PLAY x Converse heart sneaker
dates: Reported July 2020 (year inferred); article published 10 November 2020
what_happened: A small group of style creators used the hashtag HeartShoeBad to reject the sneaker, which the article says sells at 240 dollars. Videos under the tag had more than 2.1 million views. Creators said the line is known more than Kawakubo's own work and that repeated releases flooded resale. This is organic content, not a brand programme.
results_and_next_move: Neither brand has used the term or reported a response; no sales figures; the article is from an Australian outlet with no US data. Source older than three years.

initiative: CDG Homme Plus x Nike ACG Mountain Fly 2 Low
what_happened: The sneaker first appeared in the Spring/Summer 2024 Homme Plus show, then launched at Dover Street Market and CDG stores at 260 pounds. DSM New York's own page (https://newyork.doverstreetmarket.com/pages/nike-acg-comme-des-garcons-homme-plus, undated) shows sale in store and on the DSMNY E-Shop, in men's sizes 5 to 13 and women's 6.5 to 14.5.
physical_digital_bridge: Runway show first, then store and e-shop release
results_and_next_move: Results not found. Hypebae notes later sale through CDG stockists.

initiative: SoHo flagship with gallery for local artists
what_happened: First US flagship and seventh store worldwide. Interior by Rafael de Cardenas, with interactive displays and a feature exhibition with Moooi. The store includes a gallery with digital and analog spaces for experimenting and collaborating with local artists. Eyewear is sold on gentlemonster.com and through Nordstrom and Harvey Nichols.
objective: Make the store a platform for creative work and discovery and extend the brand's experiential marketing from its Korean flagships to the US.
audience: Not stated in the release. A separate Business of Fashion article (undated, written in 2016) says the brand targeted Asian millennials such as FIT and NYU students.
partners: Rafael de Cardenas (design); Moooi (exhibition); Nordstrom and Harvey Nichols (wholesale)
physical_digital_bridge: Sold directly on the website and via wholesale; no store-online integration described
investment: Not found. Store size not stated in the release; the Business of Fashion article calls it roughly 500 sq ft.
results_and_next_move: Chain Store Age counts six US stores in 2024. The brand later moved to a larger Wooster Street store (see gentle-monster-03). Source is more than three years old. No data on how the local artist gallery was used.

initiative: Grand Blue ocean installation in the SoHo store
dates: Published 26 May 2016; on display until 31 August (year implied as 2016)
what_happened: The SoHo store was turned into an ocean-themed space named after a French film. Main feature: recycled laminated glass shaped like crashing waves, plus a custom 150-gallon aquarium. Designers named: aquarium designer Justin Muir and glass sculptor Ivan Lee Mora.
partners: Justin Muir (aquarium design); Ivan Lee Mora (glass sculpture)
results_and_next_move: Shows the SoHo store being re-themed within months of opening, about 3.5 months of display. No results reported. Source is more than five years old.

initiative: Move to 70 Wooster Street and farewell exhibition at the old store
city: New York (79 Grand Street to 70 Wooster Street)
dates: Farewell exhibition 24 to 30 October (year not stated on the page; the 2026 Hypebeast article dates the Wooster opening to 2018)
what_happened: The brand left 79 Grand Street for a 6,000 sq ft Wooster Street store with giant sculptures and kinetic works that make it feel like a gallery. The old space hosted a closing exhibition called Marzipanzi: Journey to Mars, produced with Marzipanzi, theatre group La Mama and Culturehub, and an honor for architect Rafael de Cardenas.
partners: Marzipanzi; La Mama; Culturehub; Rafael de Cardenas (honored)
investment: Not found. Size of 6,000 sq ft is stated; capital and team are not.
results_and_next_move: The Wooster store remained the New York flagship through the 2026 redesign (see gentle-monster-15). The page itself is undated and gives two addresses (70 and 79 Wooster); other sources use 70 Wooster. Source is more than three years old.

initiative: Nordstrom Pop-In at select Nordstrom stores
city: Seattle, Bellevue, Los Angeles, Chicago, Dallas (plus Vancouver and Toronto)
what_happened: A rotating Nordstrom Pop-In space designed with Gentle Monster to feel gallery-like, with Korean linens and charcoal, plus virtual reality and 360-degree video of flagship stores in Seoul, Shanghai and Seattle. About 40 styles were sold, six exclusive to the Pop-In, at $215 to $305.
partners: Nordstrom (Olivia Kim leads the Pop-In series)
physical_digital_bridge: Pop-In collection sold online at Nordstrom.com/pop; VR and 360 video of flagships in store; customer data capture not stated
results_and_next_move: Not found. Wholesale partnership with Nordstrom already existed at the SoHo opening in 2016. Source is more than five years old, kept as the only wholesale partner example found.

initiative: Santa Clara flagship built around a memory theme
what_happened: A 4,300 sq ft store themed on memory, with a life-size kinetic robot of an elderly woman, a pair of moving donkeys on podiums and a kinetic pine tree held by a giant hand. Six months of design work by architects, robot designers, engineers and media and textile artists.
objective: Build a physical presence in key US markets; the US customer experience director calls stores what completes the brand's lifestyle.
partners: Not stated (in-house design team and outside specialists)
physical_digital_bridge: Not found; the article mentions no QR, app or e-commerce link
investment: Not found for capital. Six months of design work and 4,300 sq ft are stated.
results_and_next_move: Third US store at the time; the company planned five more US stores over three years. By 2024 Chain Store Age counts six US stores, and Road to VR reports eight North American stores in July 2026. Source is more than five years old.

initiative: Houston Galleria flagship with robotics lab installations
dates: Opened May 2023 (article of 25 May 2023; exact day not stated)
what_happened: A 4,800 sq ft store, described as the brand's largest in the US, with The Probe (a six-legged walking mechanical creature) and the Giant Head, a nine-foot robot face built in a year-long project by the in-house Robotics Lab.
investment: Not found for capital. 4,800 sq ft and a year-long robot build are stated.
results_and_next_move: The Giant Head Kinetic piece reappears in the 2026 New York redesign (see gentle-monster-15), which suggests reuse of signature objects across stores (inference).

initiative: Maison Margiela x Gentle Monster launch pop-up in the New York store
what_happened: First eyewear collaboration with Maison Margiela launched with pop-up installations inside Gentle Monster flagships in New York, Seoul, Shanghai, Beijing, Chengdu and Singapore, and a Selfridges corner in London. Buyers at the pop-ups received a Glam Slam print cushion as a gift while stocks lasted.
physical_digital_bridge: The official US page links to the collection shop and the campaign, so the same products sell online; the cushion gift is stated for pop-up purchases only
results_and_next_move: Highsnobiety (April 2024) says the collection sold out immediately; the claim is unquantified. A second edition followed in 2024 (see gentle-monster-08). Facts combine the MR Magazine article (6 March 2023) and the official US collaboration page (undated). Source is more than three years old.

initiative: Second Maison Margiela shoppable exhibition in the New York store
dates: Reported 27 March 2024; run dates described only as limited time
what_happened: A shoppable immersive exhibition inside the Wooster store, built on its existing alien-arrives-on-Earth storyline, with a worm-like sculpture, a crashed spacecraft, a robot greeter and a lab-coat dancer. It carried the second eyewear collection with Margiela, with leather-wrapped frames and the house's four white stitches.
physical_digital_bridge: Online link to the official collaboration story page for hours and purchasing
results_and_next_move: Edition two of a collaboration that began in 2023, which suggests a cadence of about one edition a year (inference). The official US page (undated) now calls the latest drop the fourth collaboration and lists pop-ups in eight cities, none of them New York.

initiative: Jentle Salon pop-up with Jennie in SoHo
dates: 1 to 12 May 2024; launch party Friday 3 May
what_happened: Pop-up for the third Jennie collaboration, with eight sunglass styles and 11 charms. The launch party featured a giant plush unicorn and large capybara sculptures, cocktails and influencers. The same format toured 13 cities, including Costa Mesa (1 to 20 June).
audience: Influencers and fans of the K-pop artist Jennie; Complex names three influencers at the party
physical_digital_bridge: Collection sold on gentlemonster.com; pop-up designed for social sharing per Highsnobiety (27 April 2024)
results_and_next_move: Complex says the pop-up was at the SoHo location while the official page gives 45 Grand Street, a different address from the flagship; the address is treated as a separate space. No sales figures reported. Source is more than two years old.

initiative: American Dream flagship in New Jersey

what_happened: A 4,200 sq ft store, the brand's first in New Jersey, with a facade of artwork and metal objects and lifelike moving bison. It sits in the luxury wing among Saks Fifth Avenue, Balenciaga and Hermes (Chain Store Age, undated).
audience: Not stated; the mall draws the New York metro area (inference)
partners: Triple Five Group (developer, per Chain Store Age)

initiative: Bratz x Gentle Monster Melrose pop-up

what_happened: Immersive cyber-futuristic pop-up with 21 eyewear styles, a Bratz doll collaboration, an AI booth that turns guests into Bratz dolls and a towering humanoid doll. DJ FIFI played the launch, and Nudake served tiny croissants in their US debut. Guests included members of KATSEYE.

results_and_next_move: No results reported. West Hollywood, so lower New York priority.

partners: PinkPantheress, Becky G and FIFI wore unreleased frames

The opening featured DJ Sophie Gray and food and drinks with the Mozza restaurant group.
